core_obligations: Let T be an irreducible component of X and use flatness of T_K to T to lift generalizations, so that a point of T_K generic in an irreducible component of T_K maps to the generic point of T (proof lines 1604-1608).

Show that a specialization xi' of such a point xi inside X_K also maps to the generic point of T, since no point of X specializes to that generic point, and conclude xi' lies in T_K and hence equals xi (proof lines 1608-1611).
Conclude that xi is the generic point of an irreducible component of X_K, so every irreducible component of T_K is an irreducible component of X_K (proof lines 1611-1614).
proof_roadmap: Lift generalizations along the flat morphism T_K to T (proof lines 1604-1606).
Use the absence of specializations onto the generic point of T inside X to keep xi' inside T_K (proof lines 1606-1611).
Read off the component statement for X_K (proof lines 1611-1614).
difficulty_reason: For an extension of fields K/k and a scheme X over k, the inverse image of an irreducible component of X under the projection X_K to X is shown to be a union of irreducible components of X_K (statement lines 1595-1601). The proof works with generic points: flatness of T_K to T lets generalizations lift, so a point of T_K generic in an irreducible component of T_K maps to the generic point of T (proof lines 1604-1608); the decisive step is that any specialization of such a point inside X_K must stay in T_K, because nothing specializes to the generic point of T inside X (proof lines 1608-1611). The claim is H2: one standard flatness property plus a specialization argument, but the specialization step is the part that cannot be read off formally.
